title: Replace front brake pads — 2-piston calipers
introduction:
These instructions are for the front brakes with 2-piston calipers. First expose the pads and note how the hardware is fitted. Then follow the installation details, including clip orientation, piston retraction when fitting new pads, and the final pedal and fluid checks.

The caliper must be supported while moved aside: its flexible hose is a fluid connection, not a hanger. Read the installation notes before disassembly so the top and bottom clips stay identifiable.

items.name: C-clamp and a worn brake pad
items.detail: Used to press the caliper pistons back when installing new pads.

items.name: Torque wrench
items.detail: Needed for the stated caliper guide-pin bolt setting.

items.name: Caliper support
items.detail: The original illustration shows the caliper supported while positioned aside; do not load the hose.

items.name: Correct pad kit and its supplied hardware
items.detail: Install all new hardware and lubricant supplied with a new-pad kit.

items.name: Specified brake fluid
items.detail: Use the 206-00 Brake System - General Information specifications if topping up is needed.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal instructions for installation information too; some refitting details appear alongside the removal steps.
Take off the wheel and tire using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) (204-04A Wheels and Tires, Removal and Installation).
NOTICE: Support the brake caliper when it is moved aside. Letting its weight hang from the brake hose can damage the hose.
Take out the 2 caliper guide-pin bolts, then move the supported caliper aside. The installation torque for these bolts is 24 lb.ft (32 Nm).
edits.why: Moving the caliper exposes the pads while the hose remains connected.

edits.text: NOTE: Record how the components are positioned before taking them out.
Take the brake pads out of their mounting positions.
edits.why: Keep their original arrangement clear while identifying the replacement parts.

edits.text: NOTE: The upper and lower pad clips are different. The clip with a tab belongs at the top of the anchor plate.
Remove both the upper and lower brake pad clips.
Installation — rebuild and check the brakes
NOTE: When fitting new pads, also install all new hardware and use the lubricant supplied with the pad kit. Apply the lubricant according to the kit’s instruction sheet.
Reassemble by reversing the removal operations, observing the installation notes and tightening specification given above.
edits.why: Read the new-pad piston step below as part of preparing the caliper for reassembly.

edits.text: When installing new brake pads, use a C-clamp with a worn pad to press the caliper pistons back into their bores.
edits.why: The worn pad spreads the clamp force across the pistons as shown in the illustration.

edits.text: Press the brake pedal. Check the level in the brake-fluid reservoir and add brake fluid if necessary, using [Specifications (206-00 Brake System - General Information, Specifications)](#/document/G1694687).
edits.why: Finish the pedal and reservoir checks after the brake assembly is back together.
